Getting Started with cnma

Mahmood Developer

2025-11-06

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Introduction

The cnma package provides a comprehensive toolkit for conducting network meta-analysis (NMA) with both frequentist and Bayesian approaches. This vignette will guide you through the basic workflow.

Installation 

# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("mahmood726-cyber/HFN786")

Quick Start

1. Load the Package 

library(cnma)

2. Generate Example Data

For demonstration purposes, we’ll use simulated data:

# Generate network with 30 studies and 5 treatments
data <- simulate_cnma_data(n_studies = 30, seed = 42)

# Examine the data structure
head(data)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 15
#>   studlab  treat1  treat2    TE   seTE  year is_rct study_design grade    rob2  
#>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>  <dbl>  <dbl> <int>  <int> <fct>        <fct>    <chr> 
#> 1 Study_01 Placebo DrugA  0.297 0.146   2010      1 RCT          Moderate high  
#> 2 Study_02 DrugA   DrugC  0.192 0.115   2020      1 RCT          Moderate low   
#> 3 Study_03 Placebo DrugA  0.299 0.0864  2020      1 RCT          High     low   
#> 4 Study_04 Placebo DrugA  0.693 0.189   2023      1 RCT          High     low   
#> 5 Study_05 Placebo DrugB  0.361 0.148   2013      0 Non-RCT      Low      some …
#> 6 Study_06 DrugA   DrugB  0.122 0.109   2013      1 RCT          Low      low   
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: age_mean <dbl>, female_pct <dbl>, bmi_mean <dbl>,
#> #   charlson <dbl>, baseline_risk <dbl>

The data contains: - studlab: Study identifier - treat1, treat2: Treatment comparison - TE: Treatment effect (log hazard ratio) - seTE: Standard error - Additional covariates: age_mean, female_pct, bmi_mean, etc.

3. Configure Analysis

Create a configuration object with your analysis preferences:

config <- setup_cnma(
  sm = "HR",              # Summary measure: Hazard Ratio
  use_bayesian = FALSE,   # Use frequentist approach
  use_transport = FALSE,  # Disable transportability for quick demo
  use_grade_weighting = FALSE,
  run_metareg = FALSE,
  export_plots = FALSE,
  report_html = FALSE
)

4. Run Analysis 

# Run the main analysis
results <- run_cnma_analysis(
  data = data,
  ref_treatment = "Placebo",
  config = config
)

# View results
print(results)
summary(results)

Data Format

Your data must contain these required columns:

  • studlab: Study identifier (character)
  • treat1: First treatment in comparison (character)
  • treat2: Second treatment in comparison (character)
  • TE: Treatment effect estimate (numeric, log-scale for ratios)
  • seTE: Standard error of treatment effect (numeric, > 0)

Optional columns for advanced features:

  • grade: GRADE quality (“High”, “Moderate”, “Low”, “Very low”)
  • is_rct: Study design (1 = RCT, 0 = observational)
  • rob2: Risk of bias (“low”, “some concerns”, “high”)
  • Covariates: age_mean, female_pct, bmi_mean, charlson, etc.

Network Characteristics 

# Number of studies
n_studies <- length(unique(data$studlab))
cat("Number of studies:", n_studies, "\n")

# Number of treatments
treatments <- unique(c(data$treat1, data$treat2))
cat("Number of treatments:", length(treatments), "\n")
cat("Treatments:", paste(treatments, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Number of comparisons
cat("Number of comparisons:", nrow(data), "\n")

Configuration Options

The setup_cnma() function provides extensive configuration options:

Summary Measure 

config <- setup_cnma(sm = "OR")  # Odds Ratio
config <- setup_cnma(sm = "RR")  # Risk Ratio
config <- setup_cnma(sm = "HR")  # Hazard Ratio
config <- setup_cnma(sm = "MD")  # Mean Difference

Analysis Methods 

# Frequentist only (fast)
config <- setup_cnma(use_bayesian = FALSE)

# Add Bayesian analysis (slower, requires JAGS)
config <- setup_cnma(
  use_bayesian = TRUE,
  bayes_chains = 3,
  bayes_iter = 10000
)

Advanced Features 

# Transportability analysis
config <- setup_cnma(
  use_transport = TRUE,
  transport_metric = "mahalanobis"
)

# Meta-regression
config <- setup_cnma(
  run_metareg = TRUE,
  metareg_covariates = c("age_mean", "female_pct", "bmi_mean")
)

# Quality weighting
config <- setup_cnma(
  use_grade_weighting = TRUE,
  use_rob2_weighting = TRUE
)

Understanding Results

The results object contains:

  • results$main_nma: Main network meta-analysis (netmeta object)
  • results$data: Input data
  • config: Configuration used
  • ref_treatment: Reference treatment

Heterogeneity Statistics 

# Tau-squared (between-study variance)
results$results$main_nma$tau

# I-squared (percentage of variation due to heterogeneity)
results$results$main_nma$I2.random * 100

Validation

Before running analysis, validate your data:

# Check for required columns and valid values
validate_cnma_input(data)

# Clean data (remove invalid rows)
clean_data <- cnma_clean_data(data)

Parallel Processing

For large networks, enable parallel processing:

# Enable multicore processing
cnma_parallel_on("multicore", workers = 4)

# Run analysis
results <- run_cnma_analysis(data, config = config)

# Disable when done
cnma_parallel_off()
